question: What is the apparent dip, and how is it found?
answer: A layer dipping 36° shows its full angle only in a section square to its strike. Turned toward the strike, the same layer looks flatter, and at 65° it reads about 33°. Geologists read the apparent dip off a true-to-apparent dip conversion diagram.
move: Only a section square to the strike shows the true dip; any other shows less.
